label: Builder (promoter) name
description: Legal name of the company developing and selling the project.
buyerImpact: The company you sign with and pay must be the registered promoter.
askFor: the promoter's name and company number on the registration certificate, and the same name on the agreement and every receipt

label: Buildings in this phase
description: Number of buildings (towers) covered by the project registration or advertised for the project.
buyerImpact: A building that isn't in the registration has no registered completion date or sanctioned plan yet.
askFor: the registration certificate for every building in the project, including any tower sold as a later phase

label: Floors per building
description: Floors above ground in each building (G+12 means 12).
buyerImpact: Flats above the sanctioned floor have no approved plan. Don't book them until an amended sanction is registered.
askFor: the sanctioned building plan showing the floor you are being sold, and the amended sanction if the builder claims more floors

label: Possession / completion date
description: When the project will be completed and possession handed over.
buyerImpact: The registered date is the one the builder is legally held to. Plan rent, loan EMIs and your move around it.
askFor: the registered completion date written into your agreement for sale

label: Size of a 2 BHK
description: Area of a 2 BHK apartment in square feet, as stated by the source. Registered documents must state carpet area.
buyerImpact: A bigger advertised number usually includes walls, balconies and common areas ("super built-up"). Compare prices per sq ft of carpet area.
askFor: the carpet area in sq m and sq ft written into the agreement, and the price per sq ft of carpet area

label: Amenities and common areas
description: Common areas and facilities of the project.
buyerImpact: Only registered common areas are legally promised. Advertised extras that aren't registered may never be built.
askFor: the list of common areas in the registration, and every advertised amenity written into the agreement

label: Price of covered parking
description: What the buyer pays for one covered car parking space, in rupees. Free parking is 0.
buyerImpact: Parking charged separately adds to your total cost.
askFor: the parking allotment and its price written into the agreement

label: Total cost of a 2 BHK
description: Everything the buyer pays the builder for a 2 BHK, in rupees, as stated by the source.
buyerImpact: "All-inclusive" prices often leave out parking, GST, deposits and fees. Budget for the agreement total plus stamp duty and registration.
askFor: a written cost sheet with every charge, plus stamp duty and registration, before you book

label: Environmental clearance
description: Status of the project's environmental clearance.
buyerImpact: Without environmental clearance, authorities can stop construction, which delays possession.
askFor: copies of all approvals, with the environmental clearance status in writing

label: Land area
description: Total land area of the project, in acres.
buyerImpact: Less land than advertised usually means less open space per home.
askFor: the land area and survey numbers from the registration and the title documents

label: Payment before a registered agreement
description: Share of the apartment's cost taken as advance or booking amount before a written agreement for sale is signed and registered, in percent.
buyerImpact: The law caps what a builder can take before the agreement for sale is signed and registered. Don't pay more than that up front.
askFor: a registered agreement for sale before you pay more than the legal booking amount, and a receipt for anything already paid

label: Defect liability period
description: How long after possession the builder must fix structural and workmanship defects free of charge, in years.
buyerImpact: The law makes the builder fix defects reported within five years of possession, free of charge. A shorter period in your agreement gives you less than the law does.
askFor: the defect liability clause corrected to five years from possession, as the Act requires
